learn.title: Backup design for compute, databases and unstructured data
objectives: Choose between a Recovery Services vault and a Backup vault and pick the right Azure Backup solution for VMs, disks, AKS and on-premises servers (MARS, MABS, DPM)
Design VM backup policies (Standard vs Enhanced, instant restore, retention) and restore options such as file-level, cross-region, cross-zonal and cross-subscription restore
Protect backups against deletion and ransomware with soft delete, immutable vaults and multi-user authorization (Resource Guard)
Recommend backup and restore designs for Azure SQL, SQL Server in Azure VMs, PostgreSQL and MySQL flexible servers, and Azure Cosmos DB
Recommend operational or vaulted backup for Blob Storage, Azure Files and Azure Data Lake Storage, and understand where each one can restore to
concepts: Recovery Services vault
Vault for Azure VMs, SQL Server and SAP HANA in Azure VMs, Azure Files, and MARS, MABS and DPM backups. Storage redundancy (GRS by default) can't be changed after backups are configured.
Backup vault

Vault for newer workloads: Azure Disks, Azure Blobs, Azure Data Lake Storage, Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server LTR and AKS. It uses a managed identity that needs roles on the protected resources.
Enhanced VM policy
Backups as often as every 4 hours, instant restore snapshots kept 1-30 days, zone-redundant snapshots, and support for Premium SSD v2 and Ultra Disks. A VM on Enhanced can't move back to Standard.
Instant restore

Restore from snapshots kept next to the disks before data reaches the vault. Standard policy keeps them 1-5 days (default 2), Enhanced 1-30 days (default 7). It can't be disabled and snapshots add storage cost.
Cross Region Restore
Restore VM backups in the paired region at any time from a GRS vault with CRR enabled. Only vault-tier points are replicated, so the secondary RPO can be up to 36 hours.
MARS agent
Windows-only agent that backs up files, folders and system state directly to a Recovery Services vault, up to three times a day. The encryption passphrase stays with you.
MABS / DPM
On-premises backup servers for app-aware backup of SQL Server, Hyper-V, VMware, Exchange and SharePoint to local disk, then to Azure via MARS. MABS needs no System Center licence; DPM does.
Azure Disk Backup

Agentless, crash-consistent incremental snapshots of managed disks (hourly or daily) kept in your subscription. Operational tier only, no protected instance fee, up to 450 scheduled snapshots per disk.
Soft delete and immutability
Deleted backup data is kept 14 days free (configurable to 180). An immutable vault blocks operations that lose recovery points; once locked it can't be disabled.
Multi-user authorization
Resource Guard, owned by a security admin (ideally in another subscription or tenant), must approve critical vault operations such as disabling soft delete or reducing retention.
Azure SQL automated backups
Weekly full, 12- or 24-hour differential and about 10-minute log backups. PITR 1-35 days (Basic 1-7, default 7), LTR up to 10 years, geo-restore only with geo-redundant backup storage.
Cosmos DB backup modes

Periodic: full backup every 4 hours, two copies kept free, restore by support request into a new account. Continuous: self-service point-in-time restore with a 7-day (no backup storage charge), 30-day or 35-day tier.
Operational vs vaulted blob backup

Operational: local, continuous PITR inside the source account (max 360 days), restore to the same account. Vaulted: scheduled copy into a Backup vault (up to 10 years), restore to a different account.
Azure Files backup tiers

Snapshot tier: share snapshots in the storage account with item-level restore (max 200 recovery points). Vault-standard tier: offsite copy with cross-region restore and long retention, full-share restore only.
comparisons: Recovery Services vault vs Backup vault
RSV: VMs, SQL and SAP HANA in VMs, Azure Files, MARS/MABS/DPM. Backup vault: disks, blobs, ADLS, PostgreSQL LTR, AKS. Pick the vault by the data source, not by preference.
Azure VM backup vs Azure Disk Backup

VM backup gives application-consistent, whole-VM or file-level restore and cross-region restore. Disk Backup is agentless and crash-consistent with up to hourly snapshots, cheaper for single disks, but no vault copy and no secondary region.
Standard: once a day, 1-5 days of snapshots. Enhanced: down to every 4 hours, 1-30 days of snapshots, required for Premium SSD v2 and Ultra Disks, and irreversible once applied.
Azure SQL Database vs SQL Server in a VM

Azure SQL backs itself up (PITR, LTR, geo-restore) with no setup. SQL Server in a VM uses the Azure Backup workload extension for full, differential and log backups with a 15-minute RPO and per-database restore.
PostgreSQL vs MySQL flexible server backups
Both keep 7 days by default and up to 35. PostgreSQL geo-redundant backup can be chosen only at server creation; MySQL can move from LRS to GRS later. PostgreSQL LTR uses Azure Backup with pg_dump.
Operational vs vaulted backup (blobs and files)
Operational or snapshot tier is fast, local and cheap but lives in the source account. Vaulted copies data out of the account, survives account deletion and ransomware, and supports long retention.
traps: Geo-restore of Azure SQL is disabled as soon as backup storage redundancy is changed to LRS or ZRS; data-residency choices trade away cross-region restore.
Deleting an Azure SQL logical server deletes all its databases and PITR backups; only LTR backups survive.
Immutability and vault soft delete don't cover operational backups of blobs and Azure Files, which stay in the source account.
Azure Disk Backup and Cosmos DB continuous backups are not geo-redundant protection; for a regional outage you need VM backup with CRR or extra Cosmos DB regions.
Vaulted Azure Files backup restores whole shares only; item-level restore needs a snapshot-tier recovery point.
A VM moved to the Enhanced policy can't go back to Standard, and vault storage redundancy can't be changed after the first backup is configured.
revision: VMs, SQL/SAP HANA in VMs, Azure Files and MARS/MABS/DPM go to a Recovery Services vault; disks, blobs, ADLS, PostgreSQL LTR and AKS go to a Backup vault.
Enhanced policy: every 4 hours minimum, 1-30 days instant restore, needed for Premium SSD v2 and Ultra Disks.
Cross Region Restore needs a GRS vault with CRR enabled and restores only vault-tier points.
Soft delete keeps deleted backups 14 days free, up to 180; lock the immutable vault for irreversible protection; use Resource Guard in another tenant for MUA.
Azure SQL: PITR 1-35 days (Basic 7), LTR to 10 years, geo-restore needs GRS backup storage.
Cosmos DB: periodic every 4 hours with 2 free copies; continuous 7-day tier has no backup storage charge but restores are billed.
Blobs: operational max 360 days and restores in place; vaulted up to 10 years and restores to another account.
Azure Files: snapshot tier for quick item-level restore; vaulted tier for ransomware protection, CRR and long retention.

questions.on: Recommend a backup and recovery solution for compute

opts: Assign a Standard policy and run on-demand backups
Install the MARS agent on each VM for hourly backups
Enable Azure Site Recovery with a 4-hour replication policy
Assign an Enhanced VM backup policy with an hourly schedule
questions.e: The Enhanced policy supports schedules of every 4, 6, 8, 12 or 24 hours. The Standard policy backs up once a day.

Switch backup storage to zone-redundant storage
questions.e: Geo-restore uses geo-replicated copies of backups and needs GRS or GZRS backup storage. PITR can only restore in the same region.

Increase the backup retention period to 35 days

Multi-user authorization with Resource Guard in the same subscription
